title: Nonuniform \(\mathrm{NC}^{1}\) versus P/poly
formal: Can every polynomial-size Boolean circuit be replaced by a polynomial-size, logarithmic-depth circuit?
context:
Paraphrase of a question in Communication Complexity (early author draft) (None), Open Problem 8.3. The exact definitions, parameters and assumptions must be read at the cited location. This short draft has not been developed into a self-contained research card.

The formula viewpoint asks whether polynomial-size bounded-fan-in Boolean circuits always have polynomial-size formulas. Under the standard \(\mathrm{AND}/\mathrm{OR}/\mathrm{NOT}\) basis this is the nonuniform \(\mathrm{NC}^{1}\) versus P/poly frontier, using formula balancing to compare the models.

sentences: A polynomial-size Boolean circuit represents an efficient nonuniform computation, but its longest chain of dependent gates can be large.
The question asks whether every such computation can be reorganized into logarithmic depth while retaining polynomial size.
Logarithmic depth would permit much greater parallelism without allowing an excessive number of gates.
Counting arguments and restricted circuit lower bounds do not settle this comparison for unrestricted Boolean circuits.
Resolving it would determine whether polynomial-size circuits and the nonuniform version of NC1 have the same expressive power.
